messages:
Jess: FYI the sampleapp started returning a cluster of 429s at ~18:02 when running the load script. Seems like a client-side storm from retry+prefetch.
Carlos: which SDK version? and which sample app config?
Jess: go-sdk v0.9.8 and JS sampleapp v2.3. Config attached below. Repro reliably with hedging enabled + prefetch_pages >1.
Mei: saw a similar pattern in staging with adaptive windowing too. We assumed server throttling but digging in the client shows a multiplier effect.
Ben: explanation: hedging spawns extra attempts for the same request; paginator prefetch spawns extra page fetches. Multiply them together and you get way more tokens/in-flight requests than client concurrency intends.
Alex: can you paste the minimal repro config?
Jess: sure — snippet from sampleapp.yaml:
```yaml
client:
  hedging: true
  hedging_delay_ms: 40
  max_hedges: 2
paginator:
  prefetch_pages: 4
  concurrency: 8
```
Carlos: prefetch_pages=4 * max_hedges=2 -> up to ~8 attempts per cursor advance, plus concurrency means bursts.
Ben: our telemetry counters currently increment on "request start" only for original attempts. Hedged attempts are invisible in that counter so dashboards underreport real load.
Alex: short fixes: set hedging=false in sampleapp quickstart, reduce default prefetch_pages to 1, and add a note in onboarding docs about combining hedging+prefetch.
Jess: I'm opening a quick PR to flip defaults and add a warning in the README. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sampleapp/pull/517
Infra-bot: incident created: INC-2026 - client hedging + prefetch caused request surge (assigned: eng-devex)
Mei: longer term: we should make hedged attempts consume the same client-side concurrency tickets so hedges don't exceed quotas. Also add jitter to hedging backoff and a global in-flight cap per cursor.
Ben: add e2e fault-injection that forces 429 on some requests and asserts in-flight <= configured concurrency. If it fails, block the release.
Carlos: also add a metric hedged_attempts/total_attempts and expose it in Console to detect multiplier effects in prod.
Alex: agree. Also consider a client safety policy: if server responds with high 429 rates, temporarily disable prefetch or reduce hedging automatically.
Jess: will add the metric and the quick PR. Thanks all :thumbsup:
Mei: adding a troubleshooting note to devex doc about this pattern.
Ben: learned something new today :brain:
